12	
13	# excel-author
14	
15	Produce an .xlsx file on disk using `openpyxl`. Follow the banker-grade conventions below so the model is auditable, flexible, and reviewable by someone other than the person who built it.
16	
17	Adapted from Anthropic's `xlsx-author` and `audit-xls` skills in the [anthropics/financial-services](https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services) repo. The MCP / Office-JS / Cowork-specific branches of the originals are dropped — this skill assumes headless Python.
18	
19	## Output contract
20	
21	- Write to `./out/<name>.xlsx`. Create `./out/` if it does not exist.
22	- Return the relative path in your final message so downstream tools can pick it up.
23	- One logical model per file. Do not append to an existing workbook unless explicitly asked.
24	
25	## Setup
26	
27	```bash
28	pip install "openpyxl>=3.0"
29	```
30	
31	## Core conventions (non-negotiable)
32	
33	### Blue / black / green cell color
34	- **Blue** (`Font(color="0000FF")`) — hardcoded input a human entered. Revenue drivers, WACC inputs, terminal growth, market data.
35	- **Black** (default) — formula. Every derived cell is a live Excel formula.
36	- **Green** (`Font(color="006100")`) — link to another sheet or external file.
37	
38	A reviewer can then scan the sheet and immediately see what's an assumption vs. what's computed.
39	
40	### Formulas over hardcodes
41	Every calculation cell MUST be a formula string, never a number computed in Python and pasted as a value.
42	
43	```python
44	# WRONG — silent bug waiting to happen
45	ws["D20"] = revenue_prior_year * (1 + growth)
46	
47	# CORRECT — flexes when the user changes the assumption
48	ws["D20"] = "=D19*(1+$B$8)"
49	```
50	
51	The only hardcoded numbers permitted:
52	1. Raw historical inputs (actual revenues, reported EBITDA, etc.)
53	2. Assumption drivers the user is meant to flex (growth rates, WACC inputs, terminal g)
54	3. Current market data (share price, debt balance) — with a cell comment documenting source + date
55	
56	If you catch yourself computing a value in Python and writing the result, stop.
57	
58	### Named ranges for cross-sheet references
59	Use named ranges for any figure referenced from another sheet, a deck, or a memo.
60	
61	```python
62	from openpyxl.workbook.defined_name import DefinedName
63	wb.defined_names["WACC"] = DefinedName("WACC", attr_text="Inputs!$C$8")
64	# then elsewhere:
65	calc["D30"] = "=D29/WACC"
66	```
67	
68	### Balance checks tab
69	Include a `Checks` tab that ties everything and surfaces TRUE/FALSE:
70	- Balance sheet balances (assets = liabilities + equity)
71	- Cash flow ties to period-over-period cash change on the BS
72	- Sum-of-parts ties to consolidated totals
73	- No rogue hardcodes inside calc ranges
74	
75	Example:
76	```python
77	checks = wb.create_sheet("Checks")
78	checks["A2"] = "BS balances"
79	checks["B2"] = "=IS!D20-IS!D21-IS!D22"
80	checks["C2"] = "=ABS(B2)<0.01"  # TRUE/FALSE
81	```
82	
83	### Cell comments on every hardcoded input
84	Add the comment AS you create the cell, not later.
85	
86	```python
87	from openpyxl.comments import Comment
88	ws["C2"] = 1_250_000_000
89	ws["C2"].font = Font(color="0000FF")
90	ws["C2"].comment = Comment("Source: 10-K FY2024, p.47, revenue line", "analyst")
91	```
92	
93	Format: `Source: [System/Document], [Date], [Reference], [URL if applicable]`.
94	
95	Never defer sourcing. Never write `TODO: add source`.
96	
97	## Skeleton: typical financial model
98	
99	```python
100	from openpyxl import Workbook
101	from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side
102	from openpyxl.comments import Comment
103	from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
104	from pathlib import Path
105	
106	BLUE = Font(color="0000FF")
107	BLACK = Font(color="000000")
108	GREEN = Font(color="006100")
109	BOLD = Font(bold=True)
110	HEADER_FILL = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="1F4E79")
111	HEADER_FONT = Font(color="FFFFFF", bold=True)
112	
113	wb = Workbook()
114	
115	# --- Inputs tab ---
116	inp = wb.active
117	inp.title = "Inputs"
118	inp["A1"] = "MARKET DATA & KEY INPUTS"
119	inp["A1"].font = HEADER_FONT
120	inp["A1"].fill = HEADER_FILL
121	inp.merge_cells("A1:C1")
122	
123	inp["B3"] = "Revenue FY2024"
124	inp["C3"] = 1_250_000_000
125	inp["C3"].font = BLUE
126	inp["C3"].comment = Comment("Source: 10-K FY2024 p.47", "model")
127	
128	inp["B4"] = "Growth Rate"
129	inp["C4"] = 0.12
130	inp["C4"].font = BLUE
131	
132	# --- Calc tab ---
133	calc = wb.create_sheet("DCF")
134	calc["B2"] = "Projected Revenue"
135	calc["C2"] = "=Inputs!C3*(1+Inputs!C4)"   # formula, black
136	
137	# --- Checks tab ---
138	chk = wb.create_sheet("Checks")
139	chk["A2"] = "BS balances"
140	chk["B2"] = "=ABS(BS!D20-BS!D21-BS!D22)<0.01"
141	
142	Path("./out").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
143	wb.save("./out/model.xlsx")
144	```
145	
146	## Section headers with merged cells
147	
148	openpyxl quirk: when you merge, set the value on the top-left cell and style the full range separately.
149	
150	```python
151	ws["A7"] = "CASH FLOW PROJECTION"
152	ws["A7"].font = HEADER_FONT
153	ws.merge_cells("A7:H7")
154	for col in range(1, 9):  # A..H
155	    ws.cell(row=7, column=col).fill = HEADER_FILL
156	```
157	
158	## Sensitivity tables
159	
160	Build with loops, not hardcoded formulas per cell. Rules:
161	
162	- **Odd number of rows/cols** (5×5 or 7×7) — guarantees a true center cell.
163	- **Center cell = base case.** The middle row/col header must equal the model's actual WACC and terminal g so the center output equals the base-case implied share price. That's the sanity check.
164	- **Highlight the center cell** with medium-blue fill (`"BDD7EE"`) and bold.
165	- Populate every cell with a full recalculation formula — never an approximation.
166	
167	```python
168	# 5x5 WACC (rows) x terminal growth (cols) sensitivity
169	wacc_axis = [0.08, 0.085, 0.09, 0.095, 0.10]        # center row = base 9.0%
170	term_axis = [0.02, 0.025, 0.03, 0.035, 0.04]        # center col = base 3.0%
171	
172	start_row = 40
173	ws.cell(row=start_row, column=1).value = "Implied Share Price ($)"
174	ws.cell(row=start_row, column=1).font = BOLD
175	
176	for j, g in enumerate(term_axis):
177	    ws.cell(row=start_row+1, column=2+j).value = g
178	    ws.cell(row=start_row+1, column=2+j).font = BLUE
179	
180	for i, w in enumerate(wacc_axis):
181	    r = start_row + 2 + i
182	    ws.cell(row=r, column=1).value = w
183	    ws.cell(row=r, column=1).font = BLUE
184	    for j, g in enumerate(term_axis):
185	        c = 2 + j
186	        # Full DCF recalc formula (simplified for illustration).
187	        # In a real model this references the full projection block.
188	        ws.cell(row=r, column=c).value = (
189	            f"=SUMPRODUCT(FCF_range,1/(1+{w})^year_offset) + "
190	            f"FCF_terminal*(1+{g})/({w}-{g})/(1+{w})^terminal_year"
191	        )
192	
193	# Highlight center cell (base case)
194	center = ws.cell(row=start_row+2+len(wacc_axis)//2,
195	                 column=2+len(term_axis)//2)
196	center.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="BDD7EE")
197	center.font = BOLD
198	```
199	
200	## Recalculating before delivery
201	
202	openpyxl writes formula strings but does not compute them. Excel recalculates on open, but downstream consumers (auto-check scripts, CI) need computed values.
203	
204	Run LibreOffice or a dedicated recalc step before delivery:
205	
206	```bash
207	# LibreOffice headless recalc
208	libreoffice --headless --calc --convert-to xlsx ./out/model.xlsx --outdir ./out/
209	```
210	
211	Or use a Python recalc helper (see `scripts/recalc.py` in this skill).
212	
213	## Model layout planning
214	
215	Before writing any formula:
216	1. Define ALL section row positions
217	2. Write ALL headers and labels
218	3. Write ALL section dividers and blank rows
219	4. THEN write formulas using the locked row positions
220	
221	This prevents the cascading-formula-breakage pattern where inserting a header row after formulas are written shifts every downstream reference.
222	
223	## Verify step-by-step with the user
224	
225	For large models (DCFs, 3-statement, LBO), stop and show the user intermediate artifacts before continuing. Catching a wrong margin assumption before you've built downstream sensitivity tables saves an hour.
226	
227	Checkpoint pattern:
228	- After Inputs block → show raw inputs, confirm before projecting
229	- After Revenue projections → confirm top line + growth
230	- After FCF build → confirm the full schedule
231	- After WACC → confirm inputs
232	- After valuation → confirm the equity bridge
233	- THEN build sensitivity tables
234	
235	## When NOT to use this skill
236	
237	- Users in a live Excel session with an Office MCP available — drive their live workbook instead.
238	- Pure tabular data export with no formulas — `csv` or `pandas.to_excel` is simpler.
239	- Dashboards / charts with heavy interactivity — use a real BI tool.
